Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Africa | National German companies urged to combine local production with skills training in Ghana and Africa Source : Albert Kuzor 25 November 2026 3:04pm Dr Michael Blank ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Delegate of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana, Dr Michael Blank, has urged German companies seeking investment opportunities in Africa to prioritise skills development and training alongside local production.
He said combining investment in manufacturing with efforts to equip local people with relevant skills could make a significant contribution to Africa's economic development.
Speaking to JoyBusiness on the sidelines of the German-African Business Summit (GABS) 2026 in Accra, Dr Blank said German companies must adapt their investment strategies to the needs and priorities of African countries.
He noted that supporting local production to reduce dependence on imports should go hand in hand with educating and training the workforce.
"Another thing is maybe not only to produce here, but also to educate people and to train people. So these two things, if you combine it, can really make a difference," he said.
Dr Blank observed that African countries were becoming more confident in choosing their international business partners and urged German companies to respond to those changing expectations.
He said Germany could strengthen its position as a preferred business partner if its companies demonstrated a willingness to support local industrialisation and human capital development.
"I'm quite sure that lots of German companies might look into this and see new opportunities in Ghana, but also in Africa," he added.
